## Brief description

This case addresses the challenges arising from there being several public websites for educational and career choices – [Utdanning.no](https://utdanning.no/) and [Karriereveiledning.no](https://karriereveiledning.no/) (HK-dir) and [Vilbli.no](https://www.vilbli.no/nb/no) (the county authorities, via Novari). Users – pupils, students, parents/guardians, career counsellors and job seekers – reach these through web searches and links. There is a certain overlap between the content on Vilbli and Utdanning.no, which means that some users have to make user journeys between Vilbli and Utdanning.no, even though little has been done to support this. Information on, among other things, working life, [the occupations the programmes qualify for](https://utdanning.no/interessevelgeren/yrker?utdanning=Videreg%C3%A5ende), [potential training companies](https://utdanning.no/finnlarebedrift/), [further education](https://utdanning.no/interessevelgeren/) and admission to [vocational college](https://utdanning.no/fagskolevelgeren/)/[higher education](https://utdanning.no/karakterkalkulator/) is found on Utdanning.no, while the programmes offered by each county/school are presented in most detail on Vilbli.

The case highlights the need for a single, unified channel for educational and career information that provides a simple, trustworthy and neutral route to help with choosing the next educational pathway.

### Who submitted this case?

Novari and HK-dir (the Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills), both participants in SAMT-BU.

## The problem today

Choosing an education and an occupation is among the most significant choices a person makes. Incorrect, outdated or biased information can lead to wrong choices and dropout, longer study pathways, exclusion from working life, or a poorer match between society's competence needs and the individual's choices. A lack of good information about how relevant different programmes are to working life means that educational choices are made under uncertainty.

Today there are several different public digital services for educational and career information: Utdanning.no, Vilbli.no, the question-and-answer service [Ung.no](http://Ung.no) and Karriereveiledning.no. For the last twenty years, web search – mainly Google – has distributed traffic to these services based on which of the websites the search engine has assumed to have the most relevant and authoritative answers. In recent years, commercial AI services have also used text indexed from these public websites as a source for giving (non-quality-assured) answers to users' questions about education and careers. Web search and AI services have also led to a number of advertising-funded websites based on content marketing being used as sources, displacing more objective, neutral sources online.

Because public educational and career information is split across several different websites, it has been difficult to offer good user journeys where the information is located on different websites. As a result of this fragmentation, the opportunity to offer logged-in users personalised, seamless services based on their level of education and life situation has hardly been used.

### Where do breakdowns in information flow or responsibility occur?

Breakdowns occur in particular:

- when users have no single clear entry point to public educational and career information
- when the opportunities offered by register data to show essential connections between education, competence, occupations, employers and the labour market are not used
- when editorial responsibility for overlapping content is split between different actors
- when data from the county authorities' systems (VIGO) and HK-dir's systems are not linked
- when terminology and definitions vary between the services

## Actors

### End users

- Pupils in primary and lower secondary school and students in upper secondary education who are making educational and career choices
- Students and adults in need of career guidance
- Parents/guardians
- Job seekers and employees

### Service staff

- Career counsellors in county authorities and NAV
- Counsellors and teachers in schools and upper secondary education

### Specialist system suppliers

- Suppliers of career and educational information services
- Suppliers of school administration systems connected to VIGO

### Governing actors

#### Directorates (professional and operational governing actors)

- **HK-dir** – responsible for Utdanning.no and Karriereveiledning.no; national responsibility within competence policy
- **The Norwegian Directorate for Education and Training (Udir)** – professional directorate for primary and secondary education and training
- **The Norwegian Digitalisation Agency (Digdir)** – cross-sectoral governing actor for digital interoperability and data sharing

#### Ministries (political and governance-level governing actors)

- **The Ministry of Education and Research** – overall responsibility for the education sector
- **The Ministry of Digitalisation and Public Administration** – overall responsibility for digitalisation and cross-sectoral initiatives

### Service providers

- **HK-dir** – develops and operates Utdanning.no and Karriereveiledning.no
- **Novari** – operates Vilbli.no on behalf of the county authorities
- **The county authorities** – owners of Vilbli.no through FKU (the county authorities' joint organisation for education)

### Coordinating and supporting actors

- **KS and KS Digital** – interest organisation for the local government sector; operational actor for shared digital solutions
- **Sikt** – delivers and manages shared services in the education sector

## Consequences of the current situation

### For end users (pupils, students, parents/guardians and adults)

- Have little access to personalised online services, often because some types of information are spread across different websites
- Risk of users missing essential information because the websites they visit do not have good information about relevance to working life
- Increased risk of users seeking guidance on social media and commercial AI services rather than neutral public channels

### For service staff

- Duplicated work in updating overlapping content
- Lack of overall insight into user behaviour and information needs across the services

### For organisations

- Inefficient use of resources in operating parallel solutions
- A fragmented professional community and higher overall operating costs
- Unclear lines of responsibility for content quality and updates
- It becomes expensive and difficult to develop good public AI services and personalised services if the data sources are not consolidated

### At system level

A fragmented public information landscape makes it harder to direct information towards prioritised societal needs and competence policy goals. The lack of a single unified service also weakens the potential for a comprehensive data foundation and analyses of users' choices and needs. Good personalised services require that personal data from public registers can be combined with career and educational information, so that users can be given help based on their own life situation. Because of privacy and the GDPR, personal data is unlikely to be shareable with foreign AI services. Developing future AI services for career choices will therefore require the underlying data to be consolidated.

## Desired situation

In a desired situation there is one unified public website that brings together all educational and career information – with shared terminology, a clear connection between education, competence, occupations, employers and the labour market, and easy access to neutral career guidance. The service is managed by one actor with clear lines of responsibility, one editorial team and one technical solution.

Data from the county authorities' systems (VIGO) and HK-dir's systems is shared so that users looking for information about upper secondary education find everything on one website – without having to navigate between separate services.

## Input to solution choices

The project proposal from Novari and HK-dir points to the following solution directions:

**One shared public website** – merging Utdanning.no, Karriereveiledning.no and Vilbli.no into a single unified channel with a shared editorial team and one technical solution under one governance model.

**Data facilitation as a pilot in SAMT-BU** – initially focusing on enabling the sharing of data from the county authorities' solutions (VIGO) and HK-dir's solutions, so that users looking for information about upper secondary education find it on one website.

**Joint study project** – a project between Novari and HK-dir is proposed to examine:

- the effects of a possible merger
- administrative and financial consequences
- a plan for implementation

A governance model must ensure that the county authorities retain product ownership of the relevant service areas (as with Vilbli.no today).

## Insight work

The case builds on a project proposal prepared by Novari and HK-dir in connection with SAMT-BU. Merging the career web services – Utdanning.no, Karriereveiledning.no and Vilbli.no – has been put forward as a candidate pilot in the project.

## Project objectives addressed

The case addresses in particular the following objectives:

- Simpler and more seamless user journeys for pupils, parents/guardians and staff throughout the educational pathway
- Better interoperability and information flow across administrative levels and sectors
- Lifelong learning as an overarching goal – from kindergarten to working life
- Reusable solutions and shared solutions that can be shared between actors
- A better data foundation for governance, analysis and competence policy
